subject: Hosted vs Isolated deployments — feasibility, roadmap, and temporary exception ask
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted vs Isolated deployments — Atlas feasibility question + ask from Sales

Rafael / Neha —

Quick context: Atlas Fintech (prospect) has pushed back on our hosted model because they require customer-dedicated networking and an encrypted Egress policy they can control for PCI-related flows. Sales (Rafael) is asking whether we can support an isolated hosting mode short-term while we evaluate a longer Private/VPC offering. They want:

- Dedicated VPC peering or private link to their account
- Ability to enforce egress allowlist (so traffic can only go to approved destinations)
- SOC2 evidence and a tight timeline (they are in procurement)

Can we surface a feasible short-term path (engineering + security) and capture the incremental resourcing and risk? I sketched three asks:

1) Neha — security checklist and minimum gating controls to allow an exception for a single enterprise pilot.
2) Marcus — estimate runtime/config work and how much of this is already supported by Dedicated vs Private.
3) Rafael — coordinate with Atlas and confirm timeline constraints.

I've attached Atlas' security questionnaire and an annotated sketch of a potential isolated ingress/egress pattern. Can we get initial answers by EOD Thursday? Procurement is nudging the deal.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Manager, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Atlas_security_questionnaire_v1.pdf]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Isolated deployments — Atlas feasibility question + ask from Sales

Monica — thanks for flagging. Atlas is hoping for a pilot in the next 6 weeks; procurement asked for an architecture diagram plus an operational runbook describing how we will guarantee isolation and handle security reviews.

I spoke to Sarah Park (CISO) this morning — she said they "need strong assurances on egress, key lifecycle, and audit log access for the pilot". She also asked whether we can temporarily provide a VPC endpoint model that keeps traffic off the public internet (they explicitly cannot accept multi-tenant public IP endpoints).

I'll take point on the customer coordination and can push the timeline if we need more engineering time, but procurement needs an initial answer this week to not stall.

Rafael
Account Exec — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced in-thread: Atlas_security_questionnaire_v1.pdf]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Isolated deployments — Atlas feasibility question + ask from Sales

Thanks for the context. High-level security view:

- We can entertain a strictly-scoped pilot under an exception framework, but prerequisites:
  * Customer sign-off on a limited blast radius (single tenant, limited API surface).
  * Dedicated VPC peering or PrivateLink with enforced routing tables.
  * HSM/KMS controls: keys must be customer-managed (or we provide an isolated key ring per pilot).
  * Audit/logging: we can stream audit logs to their SIEM, but need a retention agreement (our standard 90 days -> Atlas wants 1 year; legal will need to review).

- Gating items: SOC2 attestation is fine (we have it), but the egress allowlist and network topology are the main operational changes.

I attached a redline of the questionnaire and annotated required evidence. We will need 2 security engineers + 1 infra PM to support the pilot prep and validation (roughly 3 weeks of focused work to stand up the network posture and run tests).

Neha
Director, Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Atlas_security_questionnaire_v1 (redline).pdf]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Isolated deployments — Atlas feasibility question + ask from Sales

Folks — technical feasibility note:

- Short-term option (least infra lift):
  * Use a dedicated subnet + PrivateLink-like endpoint per customer in our hosted environment. That achieves private connectivity but still runs on our multi-tenant control plane.
  * Egress allowlist can be enforced at the VPC level; we can add per-tenant NAT rules.
  * Quantified work: ~2 sprints (4 weeks) for infra + runtime changes, plus 1 week for deployment and testing. Need 2 infra engineers and 1 runtime engineer.

- Long-term (Private/VPC product):
  * Full customer control plane in their VPC or a VPC-proxied deployment. Bigger investment: 3-4 months and productization work (billing, rollouts, monitoring).

Caveats: the short-term approach leaves some control-plane telemetry shared. For high-assurance customers (legal/regulatory), the long-term model is preferable. If we go short-term, we should limit the pilot to low-volume endpoints and include a sunset clause.

I've attached a one-page sketch of the proposed short-term network pattern (isolation-deployment-proposal-annotated.png) and a quick staffing estimate (roadmap-impact-notes.docx).

Marcus
Head of Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: isolation-deployment-proposal-annotated.png]

From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@atlasfintech.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: OnPrem Solutions <sales@onpremsols.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Isolated deployments — Atlas feasibility question + ask from Sales

Rafael / Monica —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the sketches. Atlas is willing to proceed with a constrained pilot under the short-term option you described provided we get all of the following in writing and available before procurement signs:

- Written runbook describing the VPC endpoint, traffic flows, and egress allowlist enforcement.
- Customer-managed keys (or dedicated key ring) and confirmation of key rotation/backup procedures.
- Audit log streaming to our Splunk instance with 1 year retention for pilot data.
- A pilot scope limited to a single production-like environment with agreed throughput limits and a 30-day sunset review.

We would like OnPrem Solutions involved for a short validation exercise (they will validate routing and performance on their side). Please send the RFC and runbook draft by Monday 22 Feb. If you can provide a short statement of risks and the temporary clause language, procurement will expedite.

Regards,
Sarah Park
CISO, Atlas Fintech

OnPrem Solutions is on-copied to help scope the validation. [Attachment requested: Atlas_security_questionnaire_v1 (redline).pdf]
